title: The developer-key listing reaches the caller with its values intact
why: GET /bot-management/developer-keys is the first management response whose data is a LIST instead of an object. Code written for objects mishandles it quietly: a Python `data or {}` turns an empty list into a dict, a decoder aimed at the wrong type yields nothing, and the call still returns without an error. The owner then sees no keys — including a live one they need to revoke. The case asserts VALUES, never field names, because names are idiomatic per language: the preview, the label and the revocation date must all arrive.
